newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sun comes out to give Brussels bourse late boost.
newsitem.headline: Sun comes out to give Brussels bourse late boost.

text.p: A flurry of buying prompted by a firmer New York start and slightly easier long interest rates emerged late on Friday to lift the Brussels bourse out of the doldrums to end with light gains, traders said.

"We spent most of the day in negative territory, with people waiting to see where the Dow would go," one trader said. "It opened higher, and that was positive. Interest rates also came back a bit and that too was positive."
Traders said it was also possible that some of the late buying was linked to the end of the two-week trading account period at the close of business on Friday.
The Bel-20 index of top shares closed 11.26 points or 0.44 percent higher at 2,592.84, with 13 blue chips up, one unchanged and six down.

However, traders said, it was difficult to see if the market would continue its rampant bull run or if increasing caution among institutional investors in particular would prompt a period of consolidation or even a correction.
"We are cautious about further developments. We are not negative, but we would like to see more consolidation," one share analyst said, adding that small buyers had been very busy on the market.
Non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere was the star of Friday's market, spending the day in positive territory.
Traders said the rise was due to a combination of the strong dollar and zinc prices and the absence of the selling pressure that beset the share in recent days.
"We still see more positive scope for Union Miniere," one trader said. UM shares ended 2.97 percent up at 3,470 francs.
A number of other dollar-sensitive stocks also rode out the market's early negativeness -- notably steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, banks BBL and Kredietbank and cement maker CBR.
Temporary employment agency Creyf's interim rose 6.3 percent to 2,855 francs. Traders said it had been lagging the market and was simply catching up.

On the down side, chemical and pharmaceutical firm UCB -- which has been very volatile in recent weeks ahead of first half results due next Wednesday -- put in a late spurt but nevertheless ended the day 0.7 percent off at 142,600 francs.
UCB is the first major Belgian firm to report, and traders said the market would use the results as an indicator for other blue chips.
